title: JSON-RPC/MCP-aware agent analysis
description: Current agent analysis assumes REST patterns (distinct HTTP method + path per operation). MCP and JSON-RPC APIs route all traffic through a single POST endpoint with the real operation in the body method field (initialize, tools/call, tools/list). Detect JSON-RPC traffic and use the body method as the operation discriminator for sequence detection, completeness scoring, and agent-report. Discovered during real testing against a Flowplane MCP server — 26 samples to POST /api/v1/mcp produced no analysis because it looked like one repeated operation.

title: Restore reverted types in schemas.ts and types.ts

title: Restore snapshot column in migration v1 DDL
description: The v1 INITIAL_SCHEMA in migrations.ts is missing the snapshot column and snapshot-based UNIQUE index on aggregated_schemas. Fresh DBs created with this migration will break all snapshot/aggregation features. Add 'snapshot INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1' and update the UNIQUE index to (session_id, http_method, path, snapshot).

title: Auto-aggregate with versioned snapshots
description: When --auto-aggregate is passed with --max-samples N, proxy stays alive and auto-aggregates every N samples as cumulative snapshots (v1, v2, ...). Enables specwatch diff between snapshots to show schema evolution. Proxy continues capturing after each snapshot. Ctrl+C triggers final snapshot of remaining samples.

title: Database schema migration system
description: No migration system exists. When new columns are added, existing ~/.specwatch/specwatch.db files fail with 'table has no column' errors. Need ALTER TABLE migrations with schema version tracker, or at minimum detect stale schema and prompt user to delete/recreate.

title: PATCH should not require all fields
description: For PATCH requests, fields should never be required (partial update semantics). Need HTTP method awareness in required field calculation.

title: Widen integer to number when both observed
description: When a field has integer and number values, should widen to just number since integer is a subset. Was creating oneOf [integer, number].

title: Epic: Calibration harness — validate JAIRF scoring via spec ablation
description: Validate/calibrate AgentReady's JAIRF spec scoring by ablation: fix backend + fix agent, vary only the spec, measure agent task success. Produces empirical signal->success weights to replace guessed JAIRF weights. Design: build-docs/plans/calibration-harness.md. Ablation not corpus (spec'd+callable+varied is empty in wild). One backend, N single-signal-degraded spec variants, one fixed agent, same task set -> regress success on signals. Specwatch=runtime telemetry; backend=ground-truth success.

(2) SCORER ACCESS: extract AgentReady scoreSpec into shared @agentready/scoring pkg (no published pkg exists per spike) - consumed by gold-spec/ablation/analysis; also unblocks spike Path 2. See new task. (3) AGENT: raw Claude tool-calling loop (no framework), one pinned model id, temperature 0, fixed system prompt -> guarantees agent=constant across variants.

title: Tag inner-object schema named 'Pet2' and inconsistently extracted
description:
Eval finding (session c7429d60). The tag shape {name: string, color: string} appears in two places:

1. Pet.tags.items — INLINED as anonymous object
2. PostPetsRequest.tags.items — extracted with $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet2'

Same shape, two representations. The extracted form is named 'Pet2' (numeric-suffix fallback because 'Pet' was already taken) — that name is actively misleading; readers will assume Pet2 is a variant of Pet, not 'a tag'.

Two issues:
- Naming: when extracting an inner shape from inside another schema, prefer a name derived from the FIELD context ('tag', from the field name 'tags') over numeric-suffixed parent name.
- Consistency: if a shape is extracted in one place, it should be extracted everywhere it appears (deep walk should fully unify, not partially).

Both are downstream of the FIX5 deep-dedup work — that fix lifted top-level dedup but didn't fully reach into array items consistently across endpoints.
close_reason: Naming fixed (Tag instead of Pet2). Inline-vs-ref consistency for parent-schema usages (e.g. Pet.tags still inlined while PostPetsRequest.tags is $ref'd to Tag) remains — filed as follow-up.

title: Polymorphic /events response flattened — oneOf/discriminator lost
description:
Eval finding (session c7429d60). POST /events accepts three discriminated variants by 'type' field: birthday, vet-visit, adoption. Each has a different required-field set (vet-visit needs vetName+treatments+cost; adoption needs newOwnerId+fee+contractUrl).

Specwatch emitted a single PostEventsRequest object with EVERY field flattened and ALL optional except 'type'. PostEventsResponse201 same problem. No oneOf, no discriminator. Generated clients have no way to express 'when type=adoption, contractUrl is required'.

This is a structural inference limitation: the engine emits oneOf only on TYPE incompatibility (string vs object), not on shape divergence within objects. But discriminated unions are extremely common (Stripe events, GitHub webhook payloads, etc.).

Fix direction: when an object schema shows clusters of co-occurring fields correlated with a low-cardinality enum field, propose oneOf branches by discriminator. Heuristic: pick a candidate discriminator (string field with cardinality between 2 and ~10), partition samples by its value, infer per-partition shape, and if branches differ in required fields, emit oneOf + discriminator.

Test data: drive-traffic.js posts 5 of each type to /events.

title: Path normalization fails for non-numeric IDs (e.g. owner_alice)
description:
Eval finding (eval session c7429d60, /tmp/specwatch-eval/generated.yaml). String identifiers like 'owner_alice' bypass path templating: /owners/owner_alice and /owners/owner_bob appear as TWO separate paths instead of unifying as /owners/{ownerId}. Both ref the same response shape (specwatch even noticed they're the same), but the path-level dedup never fires because the value doesn't trip the parameter heuristic.

Worse: the resulting schema is named 'Owner_alice' — a literal value from the path becomes a domain entity name. End users see $ref: '#/components/schemas/Owner_alice' for what should be 'Owner', which looks broken.

Fix direction: when multiple sibling paths share the same parent + share the same response shape, parameterize the differing segment regardless of value pattern. Reuse the existing same-schema detection (FIX5 dedup) as the signal. Then derive the parameter name from the parent segment (owners → ownerId).

Test data: server.js exposes /owners/owner_alice and /owners/owner_bob with identical Owner shape.
close_reason: Fixed in working-tree v0.3.4+. Verified end-to-end on pet-store eval: redocly lint 0 errors (was 1), spec validates as OpenAPI 3.1.

title: Honest assessment of v0.3.3 against ground-truth backend
description: Build a local Express server with a known OpenAPI spec (covering oneOf, enums, formats, nested objects, pagination, errors, PATCH semantics, query params, auth). Drive realistic varied traffic through specwatch proxy. Aggregate + export. Diff generated spec against ground truth across all dimensions: schema correctness, path templating, oneOf handling, confidence calibration, OpenAPI validity, breaking-change detection. File bd issues for every gap found. Goal: identify what blocks adoption.

title: Schema naming should be content-based, not first-seen-path
description: Domain dedup currently names schemas after the first endpoint that yielded them. Result observed in eval: error response shape {error, message} got named 'User' (because the first 401/404 happened on /v1/users/{id}); list-wrapper {data, total} got named 'Order'. A user reading the export sees $ref: User on a 404 and assumes the tool is broken. Fix: name shapes by content fingerprint or by detecting common patterns (objects with only error/message keys → ErrorResponse, objects with data+pagination keys → ListResponse<T>, etc). At minimum: never inherit a domain-entity name for a shape that looks like an error or wrapper.

title: Domain dedup should reach into array items and embedded objects
description: Schema dedup logic only deduplicates top-level response/request bodies. Identical entity schemas appearing inside data.items, nested objects, or embedded fields are inlined repeatedly. Eval reproduced this with User schema appearing inline 5 times across endpoints despite identical structure. Fix: recursively walk emitted schemas, fingerprint each object subtree, and replace repeated subtrees with $ref to a hoisted component.

title: Tighten enum heuristic to skip IDs and high-entropy strings
description: Current rule (≤10 distinct values across ≥10 samples) over-fires on UUIDs, SKUs, names, version strings. Reproduced in eval: orderId, sku, name, bio, version all incorrectly enum'd. Fix candidates: (a) skip UUID-shaped strings via regex, (b) compute string entropy and skip high-entropy values, (c) raise distinct-value threshold for string fields, (d) skip if any value matches /^[a-f0-9-]{20,}$/ (UUID-like). Test: SKU-style strings, UUIDs, proper names, semver should NOT become enums; status/role/currency style should.

title: Preserve 204 No Content status code in samples + export
description: Currently DELETE responses returning 204 are emitted as 200 in OpenAPI. Proxy or aggregation is silently coercing. Fix the path that records HTTP status, ensure 204 flows through to the export with no response body schema. Test: DELETE endpoint that returns 204 should appear in spec as '204: description: No Content'.

title: Detect nullable fields when null observed in samples
description: When a field is sometimes a value and sometimes null, the inference engine emits the value type only (no nullable: true / OpenAPI 3.1 type array with null). Generated clients silently break on null. Fix: track null observations during merge, emit OAS 3.1 'type: [string, "null"]' or OAS 3.0 'nullable: true' depending on output version.

title: v0.3.3 honest assessment: schema generation quality
description: Build tricky mock backend, drive 200 samples, compare export vs ground truth. Score each dimension.

title: v0.3.3 plugin quality fixes
description: Apply review findings before shipping specwatch-plugin: shell injection, stale PID kill, missing PID guard, infinite wait, no-args guard, proxy startup validation, dedup export logic, drop unused version frontmatter.

title: specwatch init: generate Claude Code plugin with skills
description: New CLI command: specwatch init. Detects project context (test command from package.json, server port, existing spec files) and generates a Claude Code plugin in .claude/plugins/specwatch/ with plugin.json and two skills: (1) check.md — API spec validation (bootstrap, validate, diff modes), (2) agent-check.md — agent traffic analysis (verification loops, redundant calls, thin responses). Both skills are always generated. The agent picks the right one based on context. Optionally includes a hook for API change reminders.

title: specwatch check: compare traffic against reference spec
description: New CLI command: specwatch check --reference <spec.yaml> [--session <id>]. Compares captured/inferred schema against a reference OpenAPI spec. Emits lint-style findings: missing endpoints, missing fields, type mismatches, breaking changes, thin responses. Uses the findings output format. Can be run standalone after a session, or invoked automatically by specwatch run --compare.

title: Lint-style findings output format
description: Define a structured finding format for specwatch output. Each finding is JSON: {severity: error|warning|info, endpoint: 'POST /users', field?: 'created_at', message: string, suggestion?: string}. Output as JSON lines (one finding per line) for easy agent consumption. Also support --format=human for readable table output. This format is used by specwatch check and specwatch run.

title: specwatch run: single-command capture + test orchestration
description: New CLI command: specwatch run <test-command> --target <url> [--port 8080] [--compare reference.yaml]. Starts proxy, runs the test command as a child process, captures traffic, stops proxy when tests finish, optionally compares against reference spec. Exit code reflects findings. This is the atomic operation that replaces start/wait/stop/export.

title: Epic: Agent-native specwatch — single-command + skill generation
description: Make specwatch usable as an agent tool. Three pillars: (1) specwatch run — single atomic command that starts proxy, runs a test command, captures traffic, compares against reference spec, outputs lint-style findings. (2) specwatch init — generates Claude Code plugin with skills so agents discover and use specwatch automatically. (3) Lint-style output format — JSON findings with severity, endpoint, message, suggestion that agents can act on without understanding OpenAPI. Dogfood by running against MockBank.

title: Tests for domain model inference and export integration
description: Write tests in tests/unit/domain-models.test.ts covering: (1) fingerprint grouping across endpoints, (2) name inference from path segments, (3) array-of unwrapping (GET /users items match GET /users/{id}), (4) collision handling when different schemas map to same name, (5) schemas with no match stay inline, (6) end-to-end: aggregated schemas → OpenAPI doc with domain model refs in components/schemas. Also add integration test showing realistic multi-endpoint API producing unified domain models.

title: Export integration: replace inline schemas with domain model refs
description: Update src/export/openapi.ts to use DomainModelRegistry. When building the OpenAPI doc, if a request/response schema matches a domain model, emit a $ref to components/schemas/{ModelName} instead of inline. Handle: (1) exact matches → direct $ref, (2) array-of matches → { type: array, items: { $ref } }, (3) schemas that DON'T match any domain model stay inline as today. Update SchemaCollector to prefer domain model names over generated operation names. Preserve backward compat: domain model dedup is additive, existing per-operation schemas still work.
close_reason: Integrated domain models into OpenAPI export with backward-compatible agentExtensions. All 971 tests pass.

title: Domain model discovery: cross-endpoint fingerprint, group, and name schemas
description: Extend computeSchemaFingerprint for cross-endpoint use. After aggregation, scan all AggregatedSchemas, fingerprint response/request body schemas, group identical ones, infer domain names from path segments (e.g. /users → User, /orders → Order). Handle array-of unwrapping: if GET /users returns array of items matching GET /users/{id} response, both map to 'User'. Create src/export/domain-models.ts with: discoverDomainModels(schemas: AggregatedSchema[]) → DomainModelRegistry. Key types: DomainModel { name, schema, fingerprint, usages[] }, DomainModelRegistry { models, lookup by fingerprint }.

title: Parse MCP text response content for completeness scoring
description: MCP responses wrap actual data in content[].text as serialized JSON strings. Completeness scoring currently sees only the JSON-RPC wrapper fields (jsonrpc, id, result), not the actual tool output. Detect when the text field contains JSON, parse it, and use those fields for write/read tool comparison. Discovered during real testing against Flowplane MCP server.
close_reason: MCP responses now unwrapped before schema inference

title: Add --consumer flag to specwatch start (human|agent)
description: Add --consumer <type> option to the start command. Defaults to 'human'. When set to 'agent', tags all samples in the session as agent traffic. This is the foundation for agent-friendly analysis — the agent-report, verification loop detection, and response completeness scoring all need to know which traffic came from agents. Store consumer type on the session row.

title: specwatch agent-report: agent-friendliness analysis
description: New command that generates a report on API agent-friendliness: which endpoints trigger verification loops, which responses are too thin, where ID/name confusion occurs (value from response used in wrong field of next request). Designed for API authors tuning their APIs for agent consumers.

title: Detect operation sequences and verification loops from traffic
description: Track request ordering per session to identify common chains (POST then GET same resource = verification loop, create parent then create children). Store as operation graphs per endpoint. This is the foundation for agent-friendly spec generation.

title: Response completeness scoring: thin vs rich responses
description: Compare POST/PUT responses against GET responses for the same resource. Flag thin responses (just ok+id when GET returns 15 fields) that force agents into verification loops. The delta is the ambiguity gap that causes agents to waste tokens re-fetching.

title: Emit x-specwatch-agent OpenAPI extensions
description: Generate agent-oriented OpenAPI extensions: response-completeness (partial/full), common-next-steps (ordered list of likely follow-up operations), verification-loop-detected flag, and identifier-mapping (which response field maps to which path/query param). All inferred from observed traffic patterns.

title: Domain model inference (Level 2  dedup)
description: Use computeSchemaFingerprint to detect structurally identical schemas across endpoints, unify under meaningful names inferred from path segments (/users → User). Handle array-of vs single object.
close_reason: Domain model inference implemented: discoverDomainModels() fingerprints schemas cross-endpoint, groups identical ones, infers names from paths (singularization), handles array-of unwrapping, integrates with OpenAPI export as shared $refs in components/schemas. 24 new tests, 971 total passing.

title: Fix auto-aggregate race condition and timing
description: Three issues in auto-aggregate: (1) server.close() runs without draining in-flight connections before runAggregation() - add drain or await. (2) Replace 500ms setTimeout waits in tests with polling/promise-based approach. (3) Fix httpProxy type - use httpProxy.ProxyServer not module namespace.

title: Rebuild diff --snapshots tests against main's diff command
description: test-engineer's commands.ts changes completely regressed the diff command (stripped snapshot-within-session features, --name option, snapshots subcommand). Discard ALL diff-command changes to commands.ts. Rebuild the diff-snapshots.test.ts tests to validate main's existing diff implementation, not the simplified replacement.

title: Add collision detection to SchemaCollector.register()
description: SchemaCollector.register() silently overwrites on name collisions (last-writer-wins). Two endpoints generating the same schema name produce a corrupted spec. Add collision detection: reuse name if schemas are structurally identical, append numeric suffix if schemas differ.

title: Add integer guard to setSchemaVersion
description: setSchemaVersion uses string interpolation in PRAGMA user_version without validating the input. Add Number.isInteger + non-negative check before interpolating to prevent latent SQL injection risk.

title: diff --snapshots parsing broken: second snapshot number consumed as positional arg
description: Commander option '--snapshots <s1> <s2>' only captures one value. Running 'specwatch diff --name bank-demo --snapshots 1 2' sets snapshots='1' and session1='2', causing 'Session 2 not found'. Fix: use variadic option '--snapshots <numbers...>' to capture both values.
close_reason: Fixed: changed --snapshots to variadic option (<numbers...>) so Commander captures both values instead of leaking the second into positional args.

title: Auto-aggregate only fires once; second batch of samples never triggers aggregation
description: When running with --auto-aggregate --max-samples 200, the first 200 requests trigger aggregation and produce snapshot 1. Sending another batch of requests does NOT trigger a second aggregation. The sample counter or trigger logic likely doesn't reset after the first aggregation.
close_reason: Fixed: added !autoAggregate guard to the maxSamples early-return at commands.ts:247. 2 regression tests added.

title: Extract schemas into components/schemas with $ref references
description: Level 1: Mechanical extraction — move all request/response body schemas into components/schemas with auto-generated names, replace inline with $ref. Level 2: Deduplicated domain models — use computeSchemaFingerprint to detect structurally identical schemas across endpoints, unify under meaningful names inferred from path segments.

title: Path parameter type inference
description: Infer integer type for path parameters when all observed values are numeric. Currently all typed as string.

title: Numeric format detection
description: Add format: double for floating-point, format: int64 for large integers. Currently only string formats detected.

title: Enum inference for low-cardinality fields
description: Detect string fields with <=10 distinct values across >=10 samples and emit enum constraints.

title: Query parameter export

title: Calib: all-bad variant never applies completeness degradation
description: all-bad manifest has runtimeDriven:false, but cli.ts:101 only auto-enables THIN_RESPONSES from entry.runtimeDriven. So 'calib:run --variant all-bad' runs with FULL response bodies — the declared completeness:0 degradation never fires (confirmed: all-bad passed 5/5 in mock). all-bad is meant to degrade everything incl. completeness. Found by Codex framing review of the calibration feature back-fill.
acceptance_criteria: all-bad runs with thin responses without needing a manual --thin-responses flag (set runtimeDriven:true for all-bad in the manifest, or have the analyzer/runner treat completeness:0 as runtime-driven); a live/mock all-bad run shows degraded response completeness.
close_reason: all-bad set runtimeDriven:true (degrades completeness) so THIN_RESPONSES fires automatically; added build-failing invariant guard (runtimeDriven iff degrades completeness) + regression test. Verified: calib:run --variant all-bad now thinResponses=true. Backend suite 94 pass.

title: Domain model openApiSchema inlines nested entities — inconsistent with usage-site $ref
description:
Discovered while closing specwatch-t4h. The Tag domain model is correctly named and $ref'd from PostPetsRequest.tags.items, but the parent Pet schema (also a domain model) inlines its tags array items rather than $ref-ing Tag. Same issue with Address inlined inside Owner.

Root cause: in buildOpenApiDocument (src/export/openapi.ts), domain models are pre-converted to openApiSchema in discoverDomainModels (src/export/domain-models.ts) WITHOUT the SchemaCollector — so the conversion has no way to emit cross-model $refs. Then collector.register(name, openApiSchema) just stores the inlined version.

Fix direction: in buildOpenApiDocument, after constructing the collector and pre-registering names, do a second pass that re-converts each model.schema using the collector + a self-fingerprint exclusion (so Pet doesn't $ref itself). Update collector to support either an excludeFingerprint param or a setSchema(name, schema) method. Then Pet's tags items would emit $ref to Tag.

Test: redocly currently warns 'Address is never used' because it's referenced only via inlined Owner.address. After fix, Owner would $ref Address and the warning goes away.

title: Nullable not detected in PATCH request body — ownerId becomes empty {}
description:
Eval finding (session c7429d60). PATCH /pets/{petId} samples include ownerId values of 'owner_alice', 'owner_bob', and null. Generated PatchPetsPetIdRequest emits:

  ownerId: {}

Empty schema = 'any value', which is much weaker than the truth (string|null). The same Pet response schema correctly emits ownerId as type: [string, 'null'] (FIX2 working there). So nullable inference DOES work in response bodies, but breaks in PATCH request bodies.

Likely cause: the PATCH-special-cased pipeline (no-required-fields treatment) drops the union-type widening too. When mixing nullable values with strings, the engine should still emit a nullable union, just not require the field.

Fix direction: keep nullable inference active in PATCH-mode; only the required-field calculation should be PATCH-aware.
close_reason: Fixed in working-tree v0.3.4+. Verified end-to-end on pet-store eval: redocly lint 0 errors (was 1), spec validates as OpenAPI 3.1.

title: Query parameter values over-enum'd to free-text (q, minPrice, maxPrice)
description:
Eval finding (session c7429d60). v0.3.4 enum-heuristic fix added a field-name allowlist + UUID/semver pattern skip for JSON body fields. Query params escape both checks.

Generated spec line 593-616 enum'd:
- q to ['B', 'Rex'] (free-text search query)
- minPrice to ['10', '50']
- maxPrice to ['200', '300']

Even though the threshold says '≤10 distinct values across ≥10 samples', query params are observed-as-strings and mixed numeric/text. The skip-list isn't applied here.

Fix direction: extend the enum heuristic skip-list to query parameters, and add: skip if all values parse as numbers (numeric query params are continuous, not enums). Also: keep the field-name allowlist active for query parameter names (q, query, search, etc. should never enum).

Note: same class as prior eval finding 'enum heuristic over-fires on IDs and free-text'. Partially fixed in v0.3.4 for body fields, but query params slipped through.
close_reason: Fixed in working-tree v0.3.4+. Verified end-to-end on pet-store eval: redocly lint 0 errors (was 1), spec validates as OpenAPI 3.1.

title: Request body schema commingles 2xx-success and 4xx-failure samples
description:
Eval finding (session c7429d60). POST /pets has 12 successful 201 calls + 4 deliberately invalid 422/401 calls (empty body, missing fields). All 16 samples were merged into a single PostPetsRequest schema.

Result: name and species are correctly required at the API level (server returns 422 if absent), but specwatch reports them as NOT required because the empty/partial bodies dragged the presence count below 100%.

Fix direction: when inferring request body schema for POST/PUT, exclude samples whose response status is in 4xx — those bodies are by definition invalid and should not influence the contract. PATCH already gets special handling (no required fields). Apply analogous filtering for POST/PUT.

Note: this is the same class of issue called out in the prior 2026-04-17 mempalace eval ('Request body schema commingles valid + invalid POST samples'). Was not fixed in v0.3.4.
close_reason: Fixed in working-tree v0.3.4+. Verified end-to-end on pet-store eval: redocly lint 0 errors (was 1), spec validates as OpenAPI 3.1.

title: Generated spec emits empty servers — redocly lint fails
description:
Eval finding (session c7429d60). redocly lint reports the no-empty-servers ERROR (1 error, 11 warnings). The exported OpenAPI has no top-level 'servers' block.

Specwatch knows the proxied target URL (e.g. http://localhost:3001) and the proxy port — should emit servers: [{url: <target>}] by default. Without it, downstream tooling (codegen, mock servers) has nowhere to point.

Other lint warnings worth addressing for adoption:
- info-license / info-contact missing (low priority but trivial to make settable via CLI flags)
- operation-4xx-response: many operations missing 4xx (only emit a 4xx if observed — can't fix from observation alone, but worth flagging in docs)
close_reason: Fixed in working-tree v0.3.4+. Verified end-to-end on pet-store eval: redocly lint 0 errors (was 1), spec validates as OpenAPI 3.1.

title: Error-only path samples create literal-path entries (e.g. /pets/abc)
description:
Eval finding (session c7429d60). Two GET requests with invalid IDs (/pets/abc, /pets/notanumber) returned 400. They appear in the spec as literal paths, NOT folded into /pets/{petId}. This bloats the spec with bogus paths.

Why: path normalization is gated on the value 'looking like an ID' (numeric, UUID-shape). 'abc' fails that test and stays literal. The normalizer never considers that the parent path already has a parameterized variant (/pets/{petId}) into which these should fold.

Fix direction: when a path segment doesn't trip the parameter heuristic, check if the parent path already has a parameterized variant — if so, treat the literal as a sample of that parameter (the value is invalid client input, but the URL pattern is /pets/{petId}).
close_reason: Fixed in working-tree v0.3.4+. Verified end-to-end on pet-store eval: redocly lint 0 errors (was 1), spec validates as OpenAPI 3.1.

title: Thin response scoring treats all missing fields equally
description: Completeness scoring reports a flat percentage (e.g., cp_create_filter at 36%) without distinguishing agent-relevant fields from irrelevant ones. Fields like configuration and filter_type would help agents avoid follow-up reads, while created_at and import_id are genuinely irrelevant for agent workflows. The score is roughly half right. Potential improvements: weight fields by agent utility, allow field relevance hints, or categorize missing fields as 'actionable' vs 'informational'. Real-world example: returning configuration and filter_type in cp_create_filter response would eliminate cp_get_filter verification calls — 3 saved calls across T2+T3+T4 scenarios.

title: False positive verification loops at scenario boundaries
description: Sequence detection misclassifies cross-scenario boundaries as verification loops. When an agent runs multiple test scenarios sequentially, the end of one scenario's verification overlaps with the next scenario's pre-queries. The 3-4s delay between them is LLM thinking time, not error-retry. Example: cp_list_filters → cp_list_filters (5 occurrences, ~3s delay) flagged as redundant but is structurally correct. Need to detect scenario boundaries — possibly via time gap thresholds or by recognizing repeated initialization-like patterns.

A phase following creation/operation that is read-heavy should be 'verification', not 'discovery'. Discovery should only apply at the start of a session or before any writes.

title: Numeric query params typed as integer when only integer values observed
description:
Eval finding (session c7429d60). minPrice/maxPrice query params got type: integer because the test traffic happened to send integer values. Ground truth: number (these accept floats — e.g. minPrice=99.50).

Same root cause as cross-endpoint type unification (specwatch-j81), but specifically for query params where the wire format is always string. Inference parses the string; should default to number for any field that COULD be decimal, since query strings carry numeric values without type information.

Conservative rule: if a query param parses as a number AND is named like a price/amount/value (Price, Amount, Cost, Value, Limit, Offset suffixes), check field-name signal too.

title: Enum threshold tuning: too low for query params, too high for body fields
description:
Eval finding (session c7429d60). Inconsistent enum behavior across this run:

- 'q' query param enum'd from 2 distinct values (over-fires)
- 'status' query param NOT enum'd despite 3 distinct values (under-fires) — sample count below threshold
- 'species' body enum'd correctly (3 values, 12+ samples) — works
- 'color' body enum'd to [blue, green, yellow] (3 values, ~30 samples) — borderline acceptable
- 'treatments' enum'd to [checkup, vaccine] (2 values) — too aggressive

The current heuristic ('≤10 distinct values across ≥10 samples') is uniform across body and query parameters. Query params have far fewer samples per parameter than body fields, so the 10-sample threshold rarely fires for them — yet over-fires for free-text where it does fire.

Fix direction: per-field-type thresholds, plus minimum-sample-count gate that scales with cardinality (need ≥3× cardinality samples before enum'ing).

title: format: int32 emitted on every integer regardless of value range
description:
Eval finding (session c7429d60). All integer fields get format: int32 — id, age, total, limit, offset, count, fee, etc. Per OAS 3.1 best practice, format should be emitted only when meaningful (range-bounded or distinct from default).

Two problems:
- Pollutes the spec with redundant metadata
- Potentially WRONG for IDs that may exceed 2^31 (DB IDs in real systems often go beyond)

Fix direction: drop format: int32 by default; emit format: int64 only when an observed value exceeds 2^31. Same for format: double on numbers — only emit when distinguishing from float matters.

title: Same field, different types across endpoints — no cross-endpoint unification
description:
Eval finding (session c7429d60). 'price' in the Pet response entity is correctly inferred as number. The PATCH request body for the SAME pets endpoint infers price as integer because the PATCH samples happened to all use integer values.

Result: the spec contradicts itself — Pet.price is number, PatchPetsPetIdRequest.price is integer. A round-trip through the API would violate the spec.

Fix direction: post-aggregation pass that unifies same-named fields across related endpoints (same path family, or same domain entity). Widen integer→number wherever the broader type is observed elsewhere. This is sampling-sensitivity insurance — without it, spec correctness depends on whether traffic happened to include floats for every endpoint.

This is also why specwatch sometimes 'looks worse than reality' to evaluators: the underlying inference is right per-sample, but doesn't reconcile across views. Affects perceived quality.
